title: MDE Plan Output Manifest Entry
description: JSONL entry shape for plans/<plan-id>/output.manifest. A pure artifact trace: it records each artifact's file path in the artifact field, plus touch state and trace context (the upstream spec instance it serves via sourceRef.refs, target via rules.ids, template, contributing features) so validation can find the right context to check it against. Do not use a path field. Verification verdicts live in evidence.md (which references these entries), never here. The root manifest/ folder is derived from these entries.

template.description: The template this artifact was shaped from (its id or method-relative path), e.g. page-spec or method/templates/design-specs/page-spec.template.md. Empty string when the artifact has no governing template (e.g. generated source). Validation Pass 3 checks the artifact against this template's shape.

features.description: Ids of the MDE features that contributed to this artifact (the source of its method intelligence). Features are the method units that compile into targets (.mde/method/features/). Validation Pass 4 reads the artifact against these features' intent. May be empty for an artifact no feature governs. NOTE: this is method features, NOT business capabilities — those are the entity/scope concept referenced by sourceRef.

sourceRef.description: A REFERENCE, not a description. `refs` MUST list the concrete upstream spec instance(s) this artifact serves — real file paths under specs/ (e.g. specs/business/entities/employee.md, specs/design/UI/pages/employee-directory.md), one per Scope Type instance the target's `## Outputs` declares. It is NOT a prose label, target name, or phase word: `"API"`, `"ARCHITECTURE"`, `"intent"`, `"BOOTSTRAP"` are ALL INVALID. `kind` names the Scope Type (entity | use-case | web-page | business-rule | role | business-capability | entity-operation | integration). Verification derives `$item.entity`/`$item.page` by reading along `refs`; an artifact whose `refs` do not resolve to a real upstream spec cannot be traced and is a defect. (Formerly named `source`; renamed to `sourceRef` to make clear it holds a reference, not a description.)

kind.description: The Scope Type the refs point at: entity | use-case | web-page | business-rule | role | business-capability | entity-operation | integration.

refs.description: Concrete upstream spec file path(s) the artifact serves. MUST resolve to real files; MUST NOT be prose labels or target/phase names. An artifact that serves several upstream specs lists them ALL — e.g. a page-spec lists its subject entity and every entity its panels render, plus its capability (specs/business/entities/employee.md, specs/business/entities/department.md, specs/business/capabilities/employee-records/overview.md), never the capability alone; a rule-enforcing code module or a rule test lists the specific business-rule it implements/tests, not only the capability. Whatever the manifest cannot see (which pages implement an entity, what code enforces a rule) it must be able to answer from these refs.

rules.description: Rule and TARGET ids this artifact traces to (e.g. RULE-CORE-004, TARGET-WEB-UI). The target(s) the artifact belongs to are carried here as the TARGET-* ids — there is no separate target field.

status.description: Lifecycle of the entry. mde evaluate writes the PLANNED set first (status 'planned', before the file exists — the ownership boundary), then flips each entry to its touch state (created/modified/deleted) as it generates the real file. 'blocked' marks an entry whose generation/verification failed (the gap stays visible). A 'planned' entry that remains after evaluate completes means the work did not finish. No verification verdicts here — those live in evidence.md.
